text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fokker receivers reveal speculative currency policy of the now bankrupt aircraft maker. (p1)
- Amsterdam Options Exchange fears chaos at expiration this Friday. (p1)
- Investors put money massively in new funds of Robeco and ABN Amro bank. (p1)
- Dutch unemployment rates decline structurally, according to OECD study. (p5)
- Economic affairs ministry decides not to sell off strategic oil reserves. (p9)
- Court rules that economic and justice ministers have to publish the list of laws that were not reported to the European Commission. (p1)
- Industrial machinery maker Stork completes takeover of Fokker Technology by buying the remaining 50 pct. (p2)
- Popularity of options in ABN Amro bank shares reaches the top three of the world. (p15)
- Union De Unie is preparing a black book on working conditions at foreign airlines in the Netherlands. (p19) TROUW
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM tickets are much cheaper abroad, according to consumer organisation. (p7)
